items.title: The inertia character is equivariant for the action of the decomposition group

items.difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that the inertia character of an extension of discretely valued fields is equivariant for the action of the decomposition group on the residue field, in the form that the value at a conjugate is the translate of the value at the original element (statement lines 33430-33439). The proof recalls the construction of the character as the residue class of the ratio between the translate of a uniformizer and the uniformizer itself, records the analogous ratios for elements of the decomposition group and for inverses, and then performs a displayed computation for the conjugate in which the triviality of inertia elements modulo the uniformizer reduces the expression to the translate of the original ratio (proof lines 33441-33468). The two substitutions at the start of the computation are what make the equivariance visible. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.
